title: Sundance shooting: Calgary police chief stands by officer who killed armed man
article: Police shot and killed a suspect accused of attacking his adult grandson in the southeast community of Sundance Tuesday morning.
The ordeal began when police found a young man bleeding outside a home along Sunmount Crescent. S.E. and an older man with an edged weapon inside the residence's detached garage about 11 a.m.
An officer opened fire on the allegedly armed man who's been identified by family as 76-year-old Bob Crowle.
"Inside, they found a vehicle running with a hose attached," Calgary police Chief Roger Chaffin said.
"Officers were confronted by a man who was outside that vehicle, within the garage ... he advanced around the car towards officers with what is believed to be a large edged weapon.
"One officer - an eight-year member of the service - fired his service pistol."
Chaffin said he stands by his officers.
"It's the most difficult thing we will do in any given circumstance," he said.
"We want our members to feel safe and feel supported when they go through this (and) in this circumstance I believe our officers did as well as they could do to resolve the situation."
Paramedics took the young man - in his 20s - to hospital in stable condition.
Police say they were first brought to the home by a brief 911 call where screaming could be heard, followed by the sound of a dial tone.
Crowle's sister Marlene said what she heard happened at the home is out of character for her brother and difficult to understand.
"He was a very gentle man," his sister said.

Neighbour Wendy Rudko told reporters she first found out something was very wrong in her quiet neighbourhood when she started to see breaking news bulletins - she called another neighbour and friend, who happened to be an eye-witness.
"She said that she had just witnessed the grandson running out all bloodied and yelling that his grandfather had just hit him with a hammer ... and that the grandfather had a gun close," she said.
Rudko described her neighbour as a good person who she saw frequently out and about.
"Just such a nice man," she said.
"He was walking in the neighbourhood all the time - he walked down my back alley a lot - out walking his dog, multiple times a day."
Hearing her neighbour is now dead after allegedly attacking his own grandson was shocking and sad, Rudko said.
The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team has been notified of Tuesday's events - the police watchdog is called in whenever police actions result in a death or serious injury.
Chaffin said it's been a difficult year for his force, with many difficult situations.
"Many times our members are dispatched to something where they believe they're attending for a certain reason and then they're suddenly faced to another situation," he said.
"That happens in a very, very short period of time with not a lot of forewarning.
"You're confronted with situations that are often times very dangerous."
